metadataReview.note: The bridge-sector locator comes from the official NIAH map record for McKenny Bridge. Hughes, Campbell and Schreibman identify this as the bridge known as Mount Street Bridge. Maynooth University documents the 26 April 1916 engagement across nearby streets and buildings; the point does not describe its full extent or any exact troop position. The existing start date is retained and no end date is added. This review establishes location and opposing local forces only; strength, losses, equipment and movements are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: NIAH record 50100535 links to the official heritage map. Its NIAHBuildings feature publishes LONGITUDE=-6.24032 and LATITUDE=53.337541; the service geometry requested in EPSG:4326 is [-6.240323698173998,53.337538505431624]. Both round to [-6.2403,53.3375]. This is a bridge-sector reference point, not a surveyed troop position or a centre of the complete battlefield. The named bridge is identified with Mount Street Bridge by Hughes et al., p. 3 note 4. No historical error radius is supplied. The separate memorial southwest of the bridge and other bridges on the canal are not used.
